notable_absence.finding: This page is the counter-example the round asked about: it calls N1QL() (`N1QL(stmt);`) but never captures a return value and never calls .close() on anything - unlike the two basicN1qlSelectStmt/basicN1qlPreparedSelectStmt demo pages in this same batch, which explicitly capture the result into `results` and call `results.close()`. The best-practice example does not follow its own rule here. This is plausibly because the statement is a fire-and-forget UPDATE with no rows to iterate rather than a SELECT, and the docs never state whether requiresExplicitClose applies to a DML-only N1QL() call - so this reads as an unstated exception rather than a contradiction, but it is not explained anywhere on the page.

cross_component_finding: The N1QL(...) call inside the handler is described as itself re-triggering the OnUpdate mutation it originated from ('This will cause recursion but it will be ignored since we ignore all non-zero TTLs') - an interaction between Eventing's mutation-listening model and SQL++'s DML that isn't visible from either component's docs in isolation. Identical to the twin's finding, confirmed word-for-word on the Server tree.
